headline: Traffic chaos in Dhaka: Students block Uttara roads after HSC exam
summary: Students gathered on the streets of Uttara, causing significant traffic disruptions following the completion of their Higher Secondary Certificate examinations.
details: Students in Uttara, Dhaka, took to the streets and blocked roads after completing their HSC examinations.
The sudden gathering of students led to widespread traffic congestion in the area, affecting commuters and vehicles.
Law enforcement agencies were deployed to manage the crowd and restore normal traffic flow on the blocked roads.
Similar celebrations or protests often occur following the completion of major public examinations in Bangladesh.
caption:
Roads blocked and traffic at a standstill. Students in Uttara took over the streets after their HSC exams.

headline_marked: Iran threatens to [[block Bab-el-Mandeb Strait]] following US sanctions
headline: Iran threatens to block Bab-el-Mandeb Strait following US sanctions
summary: The IRGC warns that fuel export corridors will be closed to all if they are not open to Iran, potentially pushing oil prices to $200 per barrel.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has threatened to close all fuel export corridors that benefit the US and its allies, following new US sanctions on Iranian ports.
Analysts suggest this is a direct hint at closing the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, the entrance to the Red Sea, potentially through their ally, the Houthi group in Yemen.
The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait is a critical global trade route connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, essential for Saudi Arabian oil exports and global shipping.
A Houthi senior official warned that if Saudi Arabia continues attacks in Yemen, they are prepared to block the strait, which could drive international oil prices up to $200 per barrel.
Tensions have escalated as Houthis launched missiles at Saudi Arabia in response to Saudi bombing of a Houthi-controlled airport, breaking a four-year ceasefire.
The US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) recently conducted a seven-hour operation attacking dozens of military installations in Iran's coastal areas and around the Strait of Hormuz.
The IRGC has declared that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until 'US sinister activities' end, claiming they have retaliated by attacking US Fifth Fleet installations in Bahrain.
The US claims that Iran has attacked seven commercial ships in the past week, resulting in approximately a dozen sailors being killed, missing, or injured.
caption:
Oil prices could hit $200 per barrel if Iran and its allies block the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has threatened to close all fuel export corridors that benefit the US and its allies, following new US sanctions on Iranian ports.

Analysts suggest this is a direct hint at closing the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, the entrance to the Red Sea, potentially through their ally, the Houthi group in Yemen.

The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait is a critical global trade route connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, essential for Saudi Arabian oil exports and global shipping.

A Houthi senior official warned that if Saudi Arabia continues attacks in Yemen, they are prepared to block the strait, which could drive international oil prices up to $200 per barrel.

Tensions have escalated as Houthis launched missiles at Saudi Arabia in response to Saudi bombing of a Houthi-controlled airport, breaking a four-year ceasefire.

The US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) recently conducted a seven-hour operation attacking dozens of military installations in Iran's coastal areas and around the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC has declared that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until 'US sinister activities' end, claiming they have retaliated by attacking US Fifth Fleet installations in Bahrain.

The US claims that Iran has attacked seven commercial ships in the past week, resulting in approximately a dozen sailors being killed, missing, or injured.
